<description>
The secp256k1 subtree is built without our hardening flags: they are on `core_interface`, which the subtree does not use, so unless the compiler enables them by default its objects miss FORTIFY, the stack protector, stack clash protection and control flow protection. On aarch64 Ubuntu 26.04 with GCC 15, the three secp256k1 objects are the only ones in the build tree without the control flow property, so master's `bitcoind` has no `AArch64 feature` note.

This PR moves the flags back to a `hardening_interface` library, which `core_interface` links (reverting 77e553ab6a), and `cmake/secp256k1.cmake` passes the subtree those its C compiler accepts. The same build then shows `AArch64 feature: BTI, PAC, GCS` on `bitcoind`. The depends libraries still lack `-fcf-protection` (#30677, #30685).
</description>

I tested it with a C compiler wrapper that rejects `-fstack-protector-all`: master builds, 09509dde1d fails to build secp256k1, and 08bd06ccd4 drops the flag at configure time and builds. The wrapper, the commands and their output: https://gist.github.com/fametrano/6c0ed42765b0fc0a0d7cc9d3ae4fceb3/0f0ddc7b9b05391659c3ed92b8a74893b263a377

I filter rather than stop configuration, so a toolchain that builds on master keeps building. secp256k1 then lacks only the flags its C compiler rejects, as Core's own targets lack those the C++ compiler rejects.
